paper_title: An FPT Algorithm for Diverse Minimum s-t Cuts
classifications: Theory of computation → Parameterized complexity and exact algorithms
Theory of computation → Graph algorithms analysis
statement: Further questions concern lower bounds. For d ∈ {1, 2}, Diverse Min s-t-Cuts is equivalent to deciding whether the input weighted graph has k distinct minimum s–t cuts. Since the problem of counting minimum s–t cuts is #P-complete by the result of Provan and Ball [22], we obtain that Diverse Min s-t-Cuts is intractable even if d ∈ {1, 2}. However, this is not the case when k is polynomial in the graph size because minimum s–t cuts can be enumerated with polynomial (linear) delay [23, 25]. Is Diverse Min s-t-Cuts NP-complete in the strong sense for a given constant d ≥ 3, that is, when k is polynomial in n?
context: We conclude by stating some open problems. In our paper, we proved that the Diverse Min s-t-Cuts problem is FPT when parameterized by k and d. However, the running time of our algorithm is superexponential. It is natural to ask whether it is possible to do better. The existing complexity lower bound of de Berg, López Martínez, and Spieksma [7] does not exclude existence of single-exponential in k and d algorithm. Furthermore, it is interesting to know whether we can get a substantially better running time for the problem on undirected graphs, as this case may be easier. In particular, we can contract all residual edges in the preprocessing step. Then for the obtained instance, it can be shown that either it is a yes-instance of the problem or the pathwidth of the graph does not exceed kd. Another natural question is whether Diverse Min s-t-Cuts admits a polynomial kernel for the parameterization by k and d. Further questions concern lower bounds. For d ∈ {1, 2}, Diverse Min s-t-Cuts is equivalent to deciding whether the input weighted graph has k distinct minimum s–t cuts. Since the problem of counting minimum s–t cuts is #P-complete by the result of Provan and Ball [22], we obtain that Diverse Min s-t-Cuts is intractable even if d ∈ {1, 2}. However, this is not the case when k is polynomial in the graph size because minimum s–t cuts can be enumerated with polynomial (linear) delay [23, 25]. Is Diverse Min s-t-Cuts NP-complete in the strong sense for a given constant d ≥ 3, that is, when k is polynomial in n? Finally, what can be said for the dual parameterization, that is, when the diversity measure is the maximum size of the intersection of two cuts? Is the problem FPT in this case? Notice that the maximum family of disjoint s-t-cuts can be found in polynomial time by the results of Wagner [26].
